input.question: What makes banks special enough to be able to hold electronic money? What is stopping people from just opening their own accounts?
input.ground_truth: Banks are tightly regulated by the government, required to follow thousands of laws and rules, and subject to constant inspection and detailed audits at any time. Therefore they are trusted to manage certain financial tasks.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What makes banks special enough to be able to hold electronic money? What is stopping people from just opening their own accounts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine a big toy box. This toy box is really, really safe, and only the grown-ups who take care of the toy box can let you take toys out or put toys in. This toy box is like a bank.

Banks are special because they keep your pretend money (like the money in your account) super safe. They have strong locks, secret codes, and smart people who watch over everything. Also, everyone agrees that the bank’s pretend money is real money, so you can use it to buy things.

If you tried to make your own toy box at home and say, “This is money!” nobody would believe you, and you couldn’t buy toys with it. Banks are special because everyone trusts them and knows they are being careful and honest.

So, you can open your own account at a bank, but you can’t just make your own bank by yourself. You need the big, safe, trusted bank to help keep your money safe and useful!
